easy.question: Who spoke to Joshua in the verse?
answers: Moses
the LORD
the people of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says 'the Lord spake unto Joshua' — the LORD spoke to Joshua.

easy.question: When is it said that the LORD spoke to Joshua?
answers: When all the people had finished crossing the Jordan
When the people were still in Egypt
When Joshua was born
easy.explanation: The verse begins 'when all the people were clean passed over Jordan' — i.e. after the crossing was completed.

easy.question: Who had crossed the Jordan according to the verse?
answers: Only the priests
Only Joshua
All the people
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly refers to 'all the people' having crossed.

medium.question: In the phrase 'when all the people were clean passed over Jordan', what does 'were clean passed over' mean in context?
answers: They had completed crossing
They had begun to cross
They stood still
medium.explanation: It indicates the crossing was finished — the people had completed passing over the Jordan.

medium.question: Why does the verse say the LORD spoke when they had crossed the Jordan?
answers: Because this marked the completion of the crossing and the start of the next instruction
Because God had forgotten to speak earlier
Because God wanted to bless the river
medium.explanation: The timing signals a transition: after the crossing was complete, new instructions were given.

To indicate a geographic location
To turn the sentence into a question

That God was unaware of the people's existence
That this is a later verse unrelated to the people

A time transition marking the start of a new scene
A tribal song about the waters

The conquest of Jerusalem

paragraphs.title: Selecting twelve and gathering the stones

easy.question: How many men were taken according to the verses?
answers: Ten
Twelve
Fourteen
easy.explanation: The text begins with 'Take you twelve men' — twelve men.

easy.question: What did the men do with the stones they took?
answers: Placed them on the bank of the Jordan
Broke them into small pieces
Carried them with them and left them at the lodging place
easy.explanation: The verses say they carried the stones with them and 'left them in the lodging place' where they stayed that night.

easy.question: From where were the stones taken?
answers: From the middle of the Jordan where the priests stood
From a nearby hill
From the tabernacle
easy.explanation: They were taken 'out of the midst of Jordan, out of the place where the priests' feet stood' — i.e., from the river at the priests' standing place.

medium.question: Why were the stones intended to be a 'sign' among them?
answers: To build a new altar
So future children would ask their fathers about the crossing
To measure the water depth
medium.explanation: The stones were a memorial so that future children would ask about their meaning and learn of the crossing.

medium.question: In the phrase 'leave them in the lodging place, where ye shall lodge this night', what does 'the lodging place' refer to?
answers: A shelter or camp where they would sleep
A large rock in the river
A garden near the river
medium.explanation: Here 'the lodging place' means the camp or shelter where they would stay for the night.

medium.question: What did Joshua tell the chosen men to do?
answers: Send them to fetch water
Order them to leave the people
Pass before the ark and each take a stone upon his shoulder
medium.explanation: Joshua instructed the twelve to pass before the ark and each take up a stone on his shoulder as a memorial.

challenge.question: What does 'the place where the priests' feet stood firm' indicate in the context 'out of the place where the priests' feet stood'?
answers: The exact spot in the water where the priests stood while bearing the ark
A special type of priestly footwear
The name of a particular stone in the river
challenge.explanation: It designates the precise location in the river where the priests stood when the ark was there — the stones were taken from that spot.

challenge.question: What repeated number appears in these verses and what does it signify?
answers: Seven — representing completeness
Twelve — representing the tribes of Israel
Six — representing sin
challenge.explanation: Twelve recurs (twelve men, twelve stones), symbolizing the twelve tribes of Israel.

challenge.question: What event were the stones meant to commemorate 'forever', and how does it relate to the covenant?
answers: Only the victory at Jericho
The building of the tabernacle at Shiloh
The crossing of the Jordan by the ark of the covenant — a sign of God's presence and covenant with Israel
challenge.explanation: The stones memorialize that the Jordan's waters were cut off when the ark passed — a sign of God's saving act and presence with Israel.

answers: Ten
Twelve
Fourteen
easy.explanation: The verse says 'twelve stones' — one for each tribe.

easy.question: Who gave the order mentioned in verse 8?
answers: Joshua
Moses
The priests
easy.explanation: The verse begins 'As the LORD spake unto Joshua' — Joshua issued the command.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites put the stones after carrying them?
answers: Back into the river
On a hill
In the camp (the lodging place)
easy.explanation: They carried the stones to the place where they lodged and laid them down there.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites carry twelve stones 'according to the number of the tribes'?
answers: To build a defensive wall
To mark and remind each tribe of the crossing
To measure the river's depth
medium.explanation: The twelve stones represented all the tribes as a memorial of the crossing for each tribe.

medium.question: In the phrase 'carried them over with them unto the place where they lodged', what does 'the place where they lodged' mean?
answers: A place of worship
Their camp
A village
medium.explanation: 'The place where they lodged' refers to their camp — the place they stayed that night.

medium.question: Who set up the twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan according to verse 9?
answers: A tribal chief
The priests
Joshua
medium.explanation: Verse 9 states 'And Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of Jordan' — Joshua is the one who set them up.

challenge.question: Where exactly were the stones placed according to 'in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark of the covenant stood'?
answers: On the riverbed beneath the priests' feet as they stood in the water
On the river bank near the camp
On a small island in the river
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates the stones were placed at the spot in the river where the priests stood carrying the ark — essentially on the riverbed under their feet.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'and they are there unto this day' mean in context?
answers: The stones were removed shortly after
The stones remained there as a memorial up to the time the text was written
The stones were moved to the temple
challenge.explanation: It indicates continuity — the stones remained as a sign until the time of writing.

challenge.question: From a cultic-historical perspective, why is it significant that the stones were set down under the feet of the priests carrying the ark?
answers: To show the memorial was sacred and marked God's presence during the crossing
So the priests could sit on the stones during the rite
To prevent the people from crossing there again
challenge.explanation: Placing the stones under the feet of the ark-bearers links the memorial to the presence of God and the priestly action during the crossing, making it a sacred sign.

easy.question: Who stood in the middle of the river according to the verse?
answers: The priests bearing the ark
The tribal leaders
The armed soldiers
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says 'the priests which bare the ark stood in the midst of Jordan'.

easy.question: What did the people do immediately after the command was given?
answers: They waited for further instructions
They hurriedly passed over the Jordan
They began to build a camp on the riverbank
easy.explanation: The text says 'the people hasted and passed over' — they hurried across.

easy.question: What passed over after all the people had finished crossing?
answers: The tribal leaders only
Only the armed men
The ark of the LORD and the priests
easy.explanation: The verse states that after the people had crossed, the ark of the LORD and the priests passed over.

medium.question: Why did the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh cross before the people?
answers: Because Moses had previously told them to do so
Because they wanted to claim Jericho for themselves
Because they happened to go ahead by chance
medium.explanation: The verse says they did as Moses had spoken to them — they followed Moses' earlier instruction.

medium.question: What does 'armed' mean in the phrase 'passed over armed before the children of Israel'?
answers: People with wagons and carts
People equipped with weapons — warriors
Those wearing festival garments
medium.explanation: 'Armed' refers to those equipped with weapons — soldiers prepared for battle.

medium.question: What does it signify that 'the ark and the priests' passed over after all the people had crossed?
answers: That the ark did not play a role in the crossing
That they crossed only after the entire people were on the other side, following the commanded order
That this was a mistake by the leaders
medium.explanation: It indicates an ordered sequence consistent with the command: the ark and priests crossed after the people, following instructions.

challenge.question: How many 'prepared for war' passed over before the LORD according to the verse?
answers: About forty thousand
One hundred thousand
A few thousand
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies 'about forty thousand prepared for war' — forty thousand.

challenge.question: What is the geographical and strategic meaning of 'the plains of Jericho' in this context?
answers: An isolated mountainous area in the north
The plain area around Jericho — a place for mustering and preparing for battle
A port city on the Mediterranean
challenge.explanation: 'The plains of Jericho' refers to the lowlands near Jericho, a staging area for the approaching battle.

challenge.question: What does the role of the 'armed' men who passed before the people indicate in the verses?
answers: They were a group of merchants who went ahead to bring supplies
They served as the military vanguard and moved to battle under the LORD's name
They were permanent settlers who did not take part in fighting

A few thousand

The people
Moses

easy.question: How did all Israel view Joshua according to the verse?
answers: Only as God's agent
As they had viewed Moses all his life
Completely different from Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says they feared him 'as they feared Moses' — they viewed him similarly to Moses.

easy.question: When was Joshua magnified in the people's eyes according to the verse?
answers: After many years
During a hard battle
On that day
easy.explanation: The verse opens 'On that day the LORD magnified Joshua' — the exaltation happened 'on that day'.

answers: Because the LORD raised him in the people's eyes, so they accepted him like Moses
Because Joshua performed exactly the same miracles as Moses
Because Moses personally trained Joshua before his death
medium.explanation: The combination of the LORD's exaltation and the people's seeing Joshua as they saw Moses shows he was accepted as the successor leader.

medium.question: What does 'magnified' mean in 'the LORD magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel'?
answers: Made him physically larger
Raised his status and reputation in the people's eyes
Weakened him
medium.explanation: Here 'magnified' means his status and reputation were elevated in the sight of the people, not physical growth.

medium.question: What clear conclusion about Joshua's status can be drawn from this verse?
answers: He was less important than Moses
He was not recognized by the people
He was acknowledged as Moses' successor leader
medium.explanation: Seeing Joshua as they had seen Moses indicates he was recognized as the continuing leader.

challenge.question: What aspect does the comparison of Joshua to Moses emphasize in this verse?
answers: That the style of leadership changed radically
That Joshua's leadership was perceived as a moral and trustworthy continuation of Moses'
That Joshua's role was entirely different
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes continuity — Joshua was accepted as a faithful successor to Moses.

challenge.question: To which historical event in Joshua is this verse connected?
answers: The sin of the golden calf in the wilderness
The prophecy of Josiah
The crossing of the Jordan
challenge.explanation: Chapters 3–4 concern the Jordan crossing and the setting up of stones — this verse follows that event.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'the LORD magnified' imply about Joshua's authority?
answers: That his authority was granted by the LORD and is therefore divine in character
That his authority came only from the people
That his authority came from being related to Moses
challenge.explanation: It indicates Joshua's authority is affirmed by the LORD — a divine validation of his leadership.

That Joshua's role was entirely different

Joshua
All the people
easy.explanation: The text refers to 'the priests that bare the ark of the testimony' — the priests carried it.

answers: The Red Sea
The Jordan
The mountain
easy.explanation: They came up 'out of Jordan' — from the Jordan River.

easy.question: What did the priests do after they came up from the Jordan?
answers: Stay in the water
Go into the wilderness
Return to their former places along the banks of the Jordan
easy.explanation: They returned to their prior positions and walked along the riverbanks as before.

medium.question: What happened immediately when the priests carrying the ark came up out of the Jordan?
answers: The people began to sing
Joshua built an altar there
The waters of the Jordan returned to their place
medium.explanation: When the priests came up, 'the waters of Jordan returned unto their place' — the river resumed its flow.

medium.question: In 'the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land', what does 'were lifted up' indicate?
answers: They were detached/broken
They were raised up onto dry ground (no longer in the water)
They were burned
medium.explanation: It means their feet reached dry ground — they were no longer standing in the water.

medium.question: Who commanded the priests to come up out of Jordan as described in the verses?
answers: The assembly of people
Joshua
A foreign king
medium.explanation: Joshua gave the command: 'Come ye up out of Jordan'.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'and they went over in the same day' (or 'as before') imply about the state of the Jordan after the event?
answers: That the Jordan remained dry and did not return
That the water returned and the river resumed its normal course
That people were confused about the river's path
challenge.explanation: The expression indicates the river returned to its usual state — the waters flowed as they had before the miracle.

challenge.question: Which earlier miraculous crossing is most directly comparable to the drying of the Jordan here?
answers: Yom Kippur
The giving of the Law at Sinai
The crossing of the Red Sea under Moses
challenge.explanation: Like the Red Sea crossing, God halted the water to allow passage — the Jordan event recalls that same kind of miracle.

challenge.question: To which tribe did the priests who carried the ark customarily belong?
answers: The tribe of Levi
The tribe of Judah
The tribe of Reuben

In the second month
On the tenth of the seventh month
easy.explanation: The verse specifies they came up 'on the tenth day of the first month'.

easy.question: Where did the people camp after crossing the Jordan?
answers: On the lowland near the river
In Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho
In the center of Jericho
easy.explanation: They encamped at Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.

easy.question: How many stones were taken from the Jordan?
answers: Seven
Ten
Twelve
easy.explanation: The text refers to 'the twelve stones' taken out of Jordan.

medium.question: According to the verses, what was the main purpose for Joshua setting up the stones?
answers: To build an altar for sacrifices
As a sign to be explained to future generations — 'when your children ask'
To mark military boundaries
medium.explanation: Joshua set up the stones so that future children would ask and be told about Israel's crossing — a memorial.

medium.question: What does 'pitched' mean in 'Joshua pitched in Gilgal the twelve stones'?
answers: To destroy
To cover
To set up or place
medium.explanation: 'Pitched' here means he set up or placed the twelve stones as a memorial.

medium.question: On which side of Jericho did Israel camp according to the verse?
answers: East (on the east border of Jericho)
West
North
medium.explanation: The verse says they camped 'in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho' — i.e., east of Jericho.

challenge.question: What is the historical significance of setting up the stones at Gilgal on the east of Jericho?

A sign of leaving the land
A marker of the beginning of their settlement in the land after crossing the Jordan
challenge.explanation: Placing the stones at Gilgal right after crossing marks the beginning of their presence in the land.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'when your children shall ask their fathers in time to come' imply about the father's role?

That the father should question his children
That the father should hide the stones
challenge.explanation: The verse assigns fathers the role of recounting and explaining the memorial to their children.

answers: Because the number related to a local agricultural event
To represent the twelve tribes of Israel
Because one stone was chosen for each month
challenge.explanation: Twelve stones symbolically represent the twelve tribes of Israel — the memorial represented all the tribes.

A marker of the beginning of their settlement in the land after crossing the Jordan

Your children
Foreign kings
easy.explanation: The verse says 'and ye shall let your children know' — the children are to be informed.

easy.question: How did Israel pass over the Jordan according to the verses?
answers: On dry ground
By swimming
By boats
easy.explanation: The verse states 'Israel passed over this Jordan on dry ground' — they crossed on dry land.

easy.question: To which earlier event is the drying of the Jordan compared?
answers: The Dead Sea event
A rolling sea
The Red Sea crossing
easy.explanation: The verses compare the drying of the Jordan to what the LORD did at the Red Sea.

medium.question: What is the purpose when the text says 'that all the people of the earth might know the hand of the LORD'?
answers: So that all nations may know God's power and fear Him
To acquire new territories by war
To set up statues commemorating the deed
medium.explanation: The action aims to reveal God's mighty deeds to the nations so they might fear the LORD.

medium.question: What does 'mighty' mean in the phrase 'that it is mighty' (referring to the hand of the LORD)?
answers: Important but not necessarily powerful
A display of strength and power
Something that endures for a long time
medium.explanation: Here 'mighty' describes God's power and strength — the LORD's effective action.

That the LORD dried the Jordan as He dried the Red Sea — a repeated act of saving power
That the event was carried out by political leaders

God's power and actions — His effective might
A geographic location

That both are separate events showing the same type of divine control over waters
That the description is purely metaphorical and not historical

Natural forces without divine action
The LORD your God
